description: need frontend developers and web developers
summary: Ghosts in the Dust is an interactive 3D archive of historic NASA missions on the Moon and Mars. Users explore textured globes, locate six landers and rovers (Apollo 11 LM, Apollo 15 LRV, Viking 1, Opportunity, Curiosity, Ingenuity), inspect their hardware in 3D, and read archival-style dossiers with sourced specifications, coordinates and end-of-mission details. It addresses the challenge by turning scattered mission records into an explorable, verified experience that keeps the legacy of past missions visible. It matters because these machines are humanity's first artifacts on other worlds, and public understanding of them is mostly limited to dates and headlines.
details:
What it does. The app shows the Moon and Mars as navigable 3D globes with a marker for each mission. Selecting a marker opens a dossier with status, landing and last-signal dates, lifespan, coordinates, technical specifications, primary mission, end-of-mission details and NASA source links. A hardware inspector loads 3D models (or labelled NASA photographs where no model exists). A guided tour, timeline and side-by-side comparison connect the six missions into one story. A "Final Hours" panel gives a clearly labelled dramatized narrative with optional browser-generated narration.

How it works. A client-only React app. Mission records live in a curated JSON file; React Three Fiber renders the globes and markers; one shared coordinate function converts latitude/longitude to 3D positions and is checked by automated tests against the sphere's texture mapping. Textures and models are served locally.

Validity. Apollo 11 specifications were audited against NASA NSSDCA records and corrected. Coordinates for all six missions are tested for hemisphere and direction, which caught two misplaced markers. Dates and datum conventions (including Viking 1's two end dates and planetocentric versus planetographic latitude) are documented. Limitations are stated openly in the README.

Benefits. Makes planetary exploration history tangible for students and the public, and shows how to present mission data with honest provenance.

What we hope to achieve. A foundation for a fuller heritage archive: more landing sites and descent stages, real orbital imagery of each site, field-level citations, and a layer on how these sites are protected.

Tools. React 18, Vite, Three.js, React Three Fiber, Drei, Tailwind CSS, Framer Motion, Web Speech API, GLB/GLTF with Draco, Vercel, Node test runner.
